description: OpenTelemetry-compatible structured logging for the dagstack ecosystem — severity, sinks, context propagation, redaction, AI-agent observability. One contract for Python, TypeScript, Go.
rules: Install with: pip install dagstack-logger (Python, pypi.org). TypeScript @dagstack/logger and Go go.dagstack.dev/logger are on the roadmap and not yet released.

Bootstrap once at startup with configure(root_level, sinks, per_logger_levels, resource_attributes); after that any module calls Logger.get(name, version) to obtain a cached logger from the global registry.
Logger names are dot-notation paths (dagstack.rag.retriever); the hierarchy follows dot-prefix. Sinks and min_severity inherit from the parent unless overridden on the child.

Severity uses the OTel 1-24 integer scale with six canonical severity_text strings: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL. Backends filter by exact match on severity_text — never invent custom strings like INFO2 or WARN_HIGH.

Bucket boundaries: 1-4 TRACE, 5-8 DEBUG, 9-12 INFO, 13-16 WARN, 17-20 ERROR, 21-24 FATAL. Primary methods trace/debug/info/warn/error/fatal use baseline values 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21; intermediate values go through logger.log(severity_number, body).
logger.exception(err, attributes) emits at ERROR severity with OTel-semconv attributes exception.type, exception.message, exception.stacktrace populated automatically.
Phase 1 ships three sinks: ConsoleSink (stdout/stderr; mode auto/json/pretty), FileSink (size-based rotation via stdlib RotatingFileHandler), InMemorySink (ring buffer for tests).
ConsoleSink mode='auto' is TTY-aware: pretty colored output on a terminal, JSON-lines when stderr is piped. Force a mode with mode='json' or mode='pretty'; never assume the default is JSON.

Sinks implement four methods: emit(record) non-blocking, flush(timeout), close(), supports_severity(severity_number). The protocol is structural — any class with the right shape is a valid sink, no base class to inherit from.

emit() must not block the caller. Local sinks (Console, File, InMemory) use a lock and synchronous I/O; remote sinks (planned OTLPSink, LokiSink, SentrySink) use a bounded queue plus a background worker, dropping the oldest record on overflow.

Multi-sink routing: configure(sinks=[ConsoleSink(...), FileSink(...)]) attaches multiple sinks; each sink applies its own min_severity filter independently and a failure of one does not affect the others.

Context propagation is automatic: on every emit, trace_id/span_id/trace_flags are read from the active OTel Context and injected into the LogRecord. Records emitted outside any span have null trace_id/span_id, never zeros.

W3C Baggage entries listed in _meta/baggage_keys.yaml (tenant.id, request.id, user.id by default) are injected as LogRecord attributes under the same key — set them once at the request entry and they propagate through every downstream log line.

Redaction is suffix-based on attribute keys (case-insensitive): *_key, *_secret, *_token, *_password, *_passphrase, *_credentials → value replaced with literal '***'. Recursion through nested maps. Body is NOT redacted — format the body without secrets.

Scoped overrides for tests and per-run audit: logger.scope_sinks([InMemorySink()]) inside a with-block (Python) swaps sinks on the original logger for the block duration; emits inside go to the override, emits outside go to the global sinks.
Use InMemorySink for assertions in tests: sink.records() returns a typed snapshot of LogRecord objects; assert against record.body, record.attributes['key'], record.severity_text directly.

Three wire formats: OTLP protobuf (binary, OTLPSink), OTel JSON (camelCase keys, string-decimal nanos, hex trace ids), dagstack JSON-lines (snake_case keys, int nanos, Canonical JSON sorted keys). The internal LogRecord is identical across formats.

LogRecord matches OTel Log Data Model v1.24: time_unix_nano, severity_number/text, body, attributes, instrumentation_scope, resource, trace_id (16 bytes), span_id (8 bytes), trace_flags, observed_time_unix_nano filled by the sink at ingest when null.

Reserved event domains split into core-reserved (always: dagstack.*, operation.*, progress.*) and extension-pack-reserved (only when AI pack loaded: gen_ai.*, mcp.*, rag.*, agent.*, prompt.*). User domains follow reverse-DNS naming.

Operations carry mandatory operation.name (snake_case stable identifier) and operation.id (UUID per instance) on every record within the operation boundary. operation.kind is one of indexing/query/lifecycle/hook/maintenance/admin.

AI-agent extension pack commits to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions conformance: gen_ai.* attribute names used as-is, mcp.* used as-is, only rag.*/agent.*/prompt.* are dagstack-specific where OTel has not stabilised a convention yet.

Body truncation defaults: max_body_bytes=4096, capture_bodies=false, hash_bodies=true. Fields matching *.content/*.markdown/*.code/*.table_json/*.html get *_truncated and *_original_bytes; privacy mode replaces them with empty string or null.
configure() is idempotent — calling it again replaces the previous setup atomically; in-flight emits complete against the old configuration before the new sinks take over.

The diagnostic channel dagstack.logger.internal carries the logger's self-errors (sink failures, buffer overflow, schema validation). It does NOT inherit sinks from root by default — preventing infinite loops if root sinks are themselves broken.

Logger methods do not raise on emit. A malformed attribute is dropped or coerced; a sink error during emit is isolated to that sink, the remaining sinks keep delivering. Only configure() raises (ValueError on invalid severity / unsupported sink type).

Graceful shutdown: register an atexit / SIGTERM handler that calls Logger.get('').flush(timeout) and Logger.get('').close(). Without graceful shutdown, buffered records in Phase 2 async sinks may be lost.

Naming across bindings: snake_case in Python (set_min_severity, scope_sinks), camelCase in TypeScript (setMinSeverity, scopeSinks), PascalCase plus Ctx-suffix in Go (SetMinSeverity, InfoCtx). Wire-format casing is independent of binding API casing.
